verdict.rationale: CoreWeave documents provisioning of bare-metal GPU capacity through the Cloud Console, Terraform, or the CKS API. The unit is a managed Kubernetes cluster with Node Pools rather than a standalone instance, and you reach running code via a generated kubeconfig and kubectl. Its pricing page markets the ability to 'quickly spin-up' on-demand capacity, but nothing documents or corroborates time-to-running in minutes. missing for 10: a single-instance on-demand provisioning flow, documented or hands-on evidence of provisioning-to-running time within minutes, independent corroboration of the end-to-end developer experience.

support.subject: As a developer, I can provision an on-demand GPU instance from the console or API and be running code on it within minutes

citations.quote: Utilize on-demand GPU instances for additional workloads when you're not looking for long-term capacity commitments.
You can create a cluster with the Cloud Console or with Terraform.
The API lets you create, list, update, and delete managed Kubernetes clusters on CoreWeave infrastructure.
Create and download a kubeconfig for a specific cluster, so you can interact with the cluster using commands like kubectl.
Quickly spin-up burst On-Demand or Spot capacity—with the flexibility of great pricing.
